this is straight f*cking gold for anyone on Claude Code

you already pay for Fable 5.1, and while Opus 5.5 does all the work it just sits there

one command puts it on your session as a senior reviewer:

/advisor fable

Opus 5.5 keeps writing the code
Fable 5.1 reads the whole session, every tool call included, and speaks up at three moments only:

> before a plan: is this the right approach?
> when the same error comes back: am I digging in the wrong place?
> before "done": what did I miss?

Fable 5.1 reviews. Opus 5.5 ships

Jev engineering does the same thing one layer down: forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to Jev in under half a second, and the big model only sees the ones that actually split

• the full tree
> Opus 5.5 on high runs the main session
> explorer reads the code
> worker edits and runs tests
> researcher pulls the docs
> all three on medium
> Fable 5.1 on call as the advisor

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:

1. Check ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents for subagents that already fit explorer, worker and researcher. Draft new ones only for missing roles. Give each model: opus, effort: medium. Skip any that pin a different model and list them.

2. Set the main session to high via effortLevel in ~/.claude/settings.json, and set advisorModel to fable.

3. Find anything that keeps the advisor off (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL, DISABLE_TELEMETRY, any variable that stops feature-flag fetching) plus CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, which overrides subagent effort. Report them, change nothing.

4. Add one rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before a large plan, when an error repeats, and before calling a long task done.

Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go"

↳

code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor

i wasn't supposed to see this and now i can't unsee it

Elon Musk posted an idea that hit 4 million views:

"Grok 
@Bot
 will not only do your purchasing, but also find & negotiate the best deal"

that's literally what Grok Bot does now. SpaceXAI built itself a negotiator called Haggle Bot, published its full prompt and left the page up. then Elon called it a gamechanger in front of 21 million people. the setup costs $0 on top of the sub:

→ create a bot from the Haggle Bot template, name it Haggler
→ before you buy anything big, drop the link in the chat. it shops it around with same-day competitor prices
→ before it writes a word, it shows you the plan: target price, opening number, walk-away point, and its next two moves if the seller refuses, counters or goes silent
→ it opens 5-10% below your target and never more than 25% off their price, so the seller takes it seriously
→ it prices every line itself, because any line left blank gets priced by the seller
→ it drafts the counter in your own inbox. nothing leaves until you tap approve

the part i keep rereading: the prompt has a list of things it must never tell the seller. how soon you need it, how many you'd take, that you've already decided to buy

your laptop stays shut. the price drops anyway

in one run it took a $14,629 order down to $6,143. 58% off, by the company that makes it, using it on itself

six months from now some people will have a bot that fought every price with them. you'll have paid the sticker price every time

hits.name: Mr. Buzzoni
hits.text:
CLAUDE + JEV ENGINEERING = THE HARNESS SKILL THAT GETS AI ENGINEERS PROMOTED IN 2026

1,000 decisions on a cold frontier model cost $605
the same 1,000 through this harness cost $0.17

the core idea:
Claude proposes, Jev answers, code decides
every step leaves a receipt

the loop:
> propose - Claude writes plans and patches, and decides nothing
> filter - code drops the routes your machine can't run before Jev ever sees them
> answer - Jev picks from code's menu with a probability, or abstains
> re-check - code checks the pick against live state. stale goes to fallback
> act - the tool runs through the normal approval path
> receipt - every step logged and replayable against a new policy

the numbers:
> 0.2s median per call
> ~$0.0002 per desktop step
> 49 of 49 WebMCP tasks passed

the key insight: "I don't know" is a real answer here
when Jev is only 38% sure, a fallback written in advance fires instead of a guess

worth stealing even if you never touch Jev:
> one decision the harness can check
> the exact options code prepared
> a defined path for when the model isn't sure
> a way to measure what actually happened

the engineer who can walk into a meeting and turn a $605 line into 17 cents is the one who gets asked to design the next system

the model got the words, Jev got the choices, and code kept the final say

TypeSafeAI engineers spelled out in their docs exactly how Jev fits inside an agent, and these patterns are perfect

one rule behind all of them: the LLM thinks, jev decides, code acts

> model routing jev picks the cheapest model that can do the step

> bulk labeling one question fanned out over a huge table, the agent reads the counts

> confidence gate act, confirm or hand it to a human. your code sets the thresholds, not the LLM

why it works: 
> ~100 ms per decision 
> $0.042 per 1M input tokens, output tokens free 
> calibrated probabilities on every answer

one LLM does the thinking. jev makes the thousand small calls in between  

save this before you wire your next agent

hits.text:
Peter Steinberger, the creator of OpenClaw, open-sourced the exact setup that keeps Claude Code and Codex on the same rules

One AGENTS.MD, 69 skills and a sync script that links them into both agents on every machine he uses. 6.6k stars, MIT.

What is inside:

> 7 rule sections, from tone to git safety
> 69 skills, each with a description the agent reads before loading it
> 4 helper scripts with zero dependencies
> 1 pre-commit hook that checks every SKILL.md
> 5 slash commands: /handoff /pickup /fixissue /landpr /raise
> 1 tools.md listing every CLI on his machines

They hand work to each other. codex-first has Claude plan and review while Codex writes the code, autoreview loops on the diff, and handoff packages state for the next agent.

Fork it, run scripts/sync-skills, and replace his hosts and accounts in AGENTS.MD with yours.

HE DROPPED 10,000 EGGS INTO A VOLCANO AND THE LAST THREE SECONDS RUINED THE ENTIRE SHOT

A helicopter carries a cargo net over a crater, and the premise reads before anything moves, so the opening works.

10,000 eggs weigh at least 1,250 lb (567 kg), making the scale plausible enough to hold attention.

Then the physics collapses:

> The eggs become sunny-side-up before a clear impact.

> Cooked eggs appear inside the helicopter, breaking spatial continuity.

> Lava can reach 1,170°C, while egg protein sets near 62-70°C. at that heat, water flashes into steam and the eggs char instead of landing intact.

> The final reaction adds noise after the payoff.

The useful lesson is that spectacle needs one clean transformation with visible cause, contact and consequence. 

If the result appears before the impact earns it, viewers stop watching the event and start spotting the render.
